title: Cross-region usage merge protocol for auditable denormalization
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem: The console backend currently mirrors and denormalizes usage events into regional read stores. When a tenant is allowed to span regions (read-only mirrors for query locality) we need a deterministic, auditable merge/resolve protocol for denormalized aggregates and per-tenant materialized tables such that: (1) cross-region writes do not cause divergent aggregates, (2) audit trails can reconstruct origin and resolution decisions, and (3) migration/evacuation workflows can reconcile stores without full replays.

Scope: Design and implement a merge protocol for multi-region usage denormalization that is: idempotent, append-first, audit-friendly, and supports per-tenant residency policies (resident-only, dual-write, read-only mirror). This applies to: daily/rolling aggregates, per-tenant counters, and denormalized event materializations stored in the analytics read layer and expo-sinks. Not in scope: historical BI backfills (>90 days) which will use the offline pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Defined wire-format for cross-region journal entries with origin metadata and monotonic region sequence
Deterministic merge behavior documented and implemented (priority rule and tie-breakers)
Unit & integration tests demonstrating idempotent merge and no double-counting under concurrent replicas
Audit log trace for each merged record that shows origin region, incoming sequence id, and resolution reason
Can run region-to-region reconciliation job to bring a quarantined region to parity within bounded time and cost
Feature-flag gated rollout with canary tenants and telemetry to detect divergence >0.1%
design_decisions: Use append-only per-tenant regional journals (topic-partition style) with region-seq numbers rather than last-write timestamps to avoid clock skew issues
Merge semantics: CRDT-inspired operate-on-tombstones for counters and last-writer-wins for non-commutative fields using region precedence table
Introduce an auditable 'resolve record' that references conflicting entries and stores chosen winner + reason in a separate audit stream
Prefer deterministic region precedence derived from tenant residency config (resident region highest, then configured failover order, then origin timestamp)
Keep materialization idempotent by including per-entry operation-id (UUID) and ingestion dedupe cache with bounded TTL
implementation_notes: Add fields to analytics journal schema: origin_region, region_seq, op_id, residency_tag, original_offset
Implement MergeService as idempotent stateless gRPC endpoint that applies merge rules and emits resolve records to audit-topic
Batch apply merges for aggregate windows to minimize write amplification; use optimistic concurrency with precondition on materialized version token
Small in-store tombstones for deletes; avoid immediate global deletes, instead emit tombstone+audit and GC via retention policy
Backpressure: when reconcile backlog exceeds threshold, fall back to per-tenant degraded mode (serve from resident region only) and alert
migration_plan: Phase 0: Schema rollout - add optional fields to journal and start emitting from producers (no reads change)
Phase 1: Shadow merges - run MergeService in shadow mode against canary tenant set and validate audit traces
Phase 2: Reconcile tool - implement region-replay util to send missing ops to target and generate reconcile report
Phase 3: Controlled switch - enable merge-on-read for 5% tenants with monitoring and rollback flag
Phase 4: Full rollout - expand to all eligible tenants after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and reconciliation success
rollout_steps: Deploy MergeService prototype to eu-west and us-east staging clusters
Select 10 canary tenants across residency modes (resident-only, dual-write, read-mirror)
Run daily diff job for canaries comparing legacy-denorm vs new-merge outputs; log divergences to Sentry and audit dashboard
If divergence >0.1% for 72h, roll back and investigate using reconcile reports
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-tenant merge audit timeline with origin_region overlays and conflict counts
